post.summary: Register a user and start a session
post.description: Creates a user and immediately starts a session for them. The username and the email address must both be unused; the address is compared case-insensitively.

409.description: Username or email address already in use

422.description: The password appears in known breaches, or the email domain is blocked from registering

post.summary: Log a user in and start a session
post.description: Exchanges a username or e-mail address and password for a session cookie. Answers the same way whether the username, e-mail address or the password was wrong.

403.description: The credentials were right and the account is banned or suspended. Answered only after the password verifies, so it discloses nothing to somebody guessing. A suspension additionally carries when it ends and why, which a ban deliberately does not.

post.summary: Log the current user out and end the session
post.description: Ends the session the request was made with and clears its cookie. Other sessions of the same user are left alone.

get.summary: Read the currently signed-in user
get.description: Reports who the session cookie belongs to. The session cookie is httpOnly, so this is the only way for a client to find out whether it is signed in and as whom.

post.summary: Request a password reset link
post.description: Sends a link that sets a new password to the account's e-mail address. Takes a username or an e-mail address, like the login endpoint. Answers the same way whether or not an account matches, so it cannot be used to find out who is registered, and does the work after responding so the timing cannot either.

200.description: Request accepted, whether or not a message was sent

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset token
post.description: Spends the token from a reset link and sets a new password. The token works once and ends every existing session, so the member signs in again afterwards. No session is started here: the link may have been read by somebody else.

410.description: The link is unknown, already used, or expired

422.description: The password appears in known breaches

post.summary: Confirm an email address with a verification token
post.description: Spends the token from a verification link. Deliberately needs no session: the link is often opened in a different browser from the one that registered. No session is started either, for the same reason.

410.description: The link is unknown, already used, or expired

post.summary: Send the verification link again
post.description: Reachable without a verified address, since it is how one is obtained. Answers the same way whether a message was sent or the resend cooldown swallowed it, and does nothing at all when the address is already verified.

200.description: Request accepted, whether or not a message was sent

patch.summary: Correct an address that has not been verified yet
patch.description: The escape hatch for an address mistyped at registration, which would otherwise orphan the account. Refuses once the address has been verified: changing a proven address has to notify the old one and offer an undo, or a stolen session could move the account to another inbox.

200.description: Address changed, and a new link sent to it

403.description: The address is already verified and cannot be changed here

409.description: Another account already uses this address

post.summary: Ask to move the account to another email address
post.description: Requires the current password. Changes nothing yet: a link goes to the new address, and the account keeps the old one until that link is opened. The old address is told at the same time and can cancel.

200.description: Change requested, and a link sent to the new address

409.description: Another account already uses this address

post.summary: Apply a requested email address change
post.description: Spends the token from the link sent to the new address, which is what actually moves the account. Every session ends, including the one that asked. Needs no session of its own: the link is usually opened in the new address's mailbox, on whatever device that happens to be.

200.description: The account now uses the new address

409.description: Another account took this address while the link was outstanding

410.description: The link is unknown, already used, cancelled, or expired

post.summary: Call off a requested email address change
post.description: The link from the notice sent to the address being moved away from. Needs no session, deliberately: the person who should be able to stop this is whoever reads that mailbox, and in the case worth defending against they are not the one holding the session.

post.summary: Ask to delete the account
post.description: Requires the current password. Deletes nothing yet: a link goes to the address on file, and the account lives until that link is opened. Reachable with an unverified address: somebody who mistyped theirs must still be able to leave.

200.description: Deletion requested, and a link sent to the address on file

post.summary: Delete the account for good
post.description: Spends the token from the mailed link, which is what actually deletes the account. Needs no session of its own, and would not survive using one: the account and every session it had are gone when this returns.

410.description: The link is unknown, already used, or expired

get.summary: List the member's own sessions
get.description: Every session of the requesting member that has not expired, newest first, with the one asking marked. A session ends by itself 24 hours after its last use.

delete.summary: End every session but this one
delete.description: Signs the member out everywhere else and leaves the session asking alone — signing somebody out of the tab they are working in punishes good hygiene. No password: this is the defensive act, and asking for one blocks the case it exists for.

delete.summary: End one of the member's own sessions
delete.description: Scoped to the requesting member, so an id alone cannot end somebody else's session. Ending the session asking is allowed: it is the same as signing out.

404.description: The member has no session with this id

patch.summary: Change the password while signed in
patch.description: Requires the current password, so a session that was not the member's cannot lock them out of their own account. Every other session ends and any outstanding reset link stops working; this session survives.

422.description: The password appears in known breaches

post.summary: Create a group, with the creating user as its administrator
post.description: Creates a writing group and joins the creating user to it as its administrator. Groups are private unless the request asks for a public one.

query.summary: List groups, by default the current user's own
query.description: Returns a page of groups, by default the ones the current user has joined. The membership filter selects invitations, public groups they are not in, or everything they may see instead.

membership.description: Which groups relative to the caller: ones they have joined, ones they have been invited to, public ones they are not in, or everything they may see.

get.summary: Fetch a public group, or a private one the user belongs to
get.description: Returns a single group. A private group the current user does not belong to is reported as missing rather than forbidden, so that its existence stays hidden.

404.description: No such group, or it is private and not the user's

patch.summary: Update a group the user administers
patch.description: Changes a group's title, description or visibility. Only an administrator of the group may do so, and only one who has joined it.

403.description: The user is not an administrator of the group

404.description: No such group, or it is private and not the user's

post.summary: Start a conversation with a public group's administrators
post.description: For asking into a group found through discovery: creates a chat titled after the group and invites every joined administrator. Each has to accept before anything is read — there is no join request, only people talking.

201.description: The new chat, with the administrators invited

403.description: Already in the group, or already invited and holding an answerable invitation

404.description: No group the reader may see has this id

409.description: The group has no joined administrator to talk to

post.summary: Add a folder to a group
post.description: Nests under `parentFolderId`, or sits at the root without one. At most 5 levels deep.

403.description: Only writers and administrators can add folders

404.description: No such group, or no such parent folder in it

422.description: The parent is already at the deepest level

get.summary: List a group's folders
get.description: Every folder of the group in creation order, flat. Readable by whoever may see the group, which for a public group includes non-members.

404.description: No such group, or it is private and not the user's

put.summary: Rename a folder, or change what it says
put.description: Where a folder sits is not changed here — moving one is its own operation.

403.description: Only writers and administrators can change a folder

404.description: No such group or folder, or the group is not the user's

delete.summary: Delete an empty folder
delete.description: Only an empty one: deleting a folder with anything in it would take writing with it, and there is no history to recover it from. Empty it first.

403.description: Only writers and administrators can delete a folder

404.description: No such group or folder, or the group is not the user's

409.description: The folder still holds a folder, a page or a thread

put.summary: Move a folder under another one, or to the root
put.description: Everything inside it moves with it. Refused when the target is the folder itself or something inside it, and when the subtree would reach past 5 levels — which depends on its deepest descendant, not on the folder.

403.description: Only writers and administrators can move a folder

404.description: No such group or folder, or no such target in the group

422.description: The target is inside it, or the subtree would be too deep

post.summary: Invite a user to a group the current user administers
post.description: Invites a user to the group with a role. The invitation always starts as such; only the invited user can turn it into a membership.

403.description: The user is not an administrator of the group

404.description: No such group, or no such user to invite

409.description: The user is already invited to or a member of the group

get.summary: List the memberships and invitations of a group
get.description: Every membership of the group, invitations included, in one answer. Not paged: a member missing from the list of who is in a group is worse than a long list.

404.description: No such group, or it is private and not the user's

post.summary: Accept the current user's invitation to a group
post.description: Turns the current user's invitation into a membership. Only the invited user can accept, and only once.

404.description: The current user has no invitation to this group

409.description: The invitation has already been accepted

patch.summary: Change a member's role in a group the current user administers
patch.description: Changes a member's role. The status cannot be changed here: accepting an invitation is the invited user's to do.

403.description: The user is not an administrator of the group

404.description: No such group, or no such membership

delete.summary: Leave a group, or remove a member the current user administers
delete.description: Removes a membership or a pending invitation: one's own, which also declines an invitation, or anybody's for an administrator of the group. Removing the last remaining member deletes the group along with it.

403.description: Not the current user's own membership, and not an administrator

404.description: No such group, or no such membership

post.summary: Add a page to a group
post.description: Pages hold material the group revises — a place, a character, a rule — rather than a conversation.

403.description: Only writers and administrators can add pages

404.description: No such group, or no such folder in it

get.summary: List a group's pages
get.description: Titles in the order they were made, without their prose. Readable by whoever may see the group, which for a public group includes non-members.

404.description: No such group, or it is private and not the user's

get.summary: Read a page
get.description: The page with its prose. Its `lastActivityAt` is what an edit has to be sent back with.

404.description: No such group or page, or the group is not the user's

put.summary: Save a page the current user wrote or administers
put.description: Refused with 409 when somebody else saved since the page was loaded, so an edit cannot be overwritten unseen. Any writer or administrator may change it: a page is material the group keeps, not a post that belongs to whoever wrote it.

loadedAt.description: The page's `lastActivityAt` as it was received, unchanged: it is compared exactly, and a round trip through a date type drops the microseconds and refuses every save.

403.description: Only writers and administrators can change a page

404.description: No such group or page, or the group is not the user's

409.description: The page was saved by somebody else in the meantime

delete.summary: Delete a page

403.description: Only writers and administrators can delete a page

404.description: No such group or page, or the group is not the user's

put.summary: Move a page into a folder, or to the root
put.description: Does not count as writing in it: the page keeps the activity time it had, so it stays where it was in the order and still reports when it was last edited.

403.description: Only writers and administrators can move a page

404.description: No such group or page, or no such folder in the group

post.summary: Add a next step

403.description: Only writers and administrators can add steps

404.description: No such group, or it is private and not the user's

get.summary: List a group's next steps
get.description: Open steps by age, then completed ones by completion. Readable by whoever may see the group, which for a public group includes non-members.

404.description: No such group, or it is private and not the user's

patch.summary: Tick a step off, or reopen it
patch.description: Idempotent in both directions. Ticking an already-completed step changes nothing, so the first completer wins.

200.description: The step in its current state

403.description: Only writers and administrators can tick steps

404.description: No such group or step, or the group is not the user's

delete.summary: Delete a step the current user created or administers
delete.description: Completed steps are never removed on their own; this is the only way one leaves.

403.description: Only the creator or an administrator may delete it

404.description: No such group or step, or the group is not the user's

post.summary: Start a thread in a group the current user writes in
post.description: Starts a thread in the group. Writers and administrators may start threads; readers may not.

404.description: No such group, or the user is not a member of it

get.summary: List the threads of a group the current user belongs to
get.description: Every thread of the group, most recently written in first. Not paged: the tab strip these fill is the only way between threads.

404.description: No such group, or the user is not a member of it

get.summary: Fetch a thread of a group the current user belongs to
get.description: Returns a single thread of the group. A thread id belonging to another group is reported as missing.

404.description: No such group or thread, or the user is not a member

patch.summary: Rename a thread the current user wrote or administers
patch.description: Renames a thread. Only the member who started it, or an administrator of the group, may change it.

403.description: Only the author or an administrator may change it

404.description: No such group or thread, or the user is not a member

delete.summary: Delete a thread the current user wrote or administers
delete.description: Deletes a thread and every post in it. Only the member who started it, or an administrator of the group, may delete it.

200.description: The thread and its posts were deleted

403.description: Only the author or an administrator may delete it

404.description: No such group or thread, or the user is not a member

post.summary: Add a post to a thread in a group the current user writes in
post.description: Adds a post to the thread, either published or as a draft. Writers and administrators may write posts; readers may not.

404.description: No such group or thread, or the user is not a member

query.summary: List the posts of a thread, plus the current user's own drafts
query.description: Returns a page of the thread's published posts, plus the current user's own unpublished drafts. Other members' drafts are never included.

404.description: No such group or thread, or the user is not a member

get.summary: Fetch a post of a thread the current user can read
get.description: Returns a single post. Another member's unpublished draft is reported as missing, including to administrators.

404.description: No such post, or it is somebody else's unpublished draft

patch.summary: Edit or publish a post the current user wrote or administers
patch.description: Edits a post's text, or publishes a draft by clearing its draft flag. Only its author, or an administrator of the group, may change it.

403.description: Only the author or an administrator may change it

404.description: No such post, or it is somebody else's unpublished draft

delete.summary: Delete a post the current user wrote or administers
delete.description: Deletes a post. Only its author, or an administrator of the group, may delete it.

403.description: Only the author or an administrator may delete it

404.description: No such post, or it is somebody else's unpublished draft

put.summary: Move a thread into a folder, or to the root
put.description: Does not count as activity in the thread or in its group: moving something is not writing in it, so neither is reordered.

403.description: Only the creator or an administrator may move it

404.description: No such group or thread, or no such folder in the group

get.summary: Report whether the application and its databases are usable
get.description: Reports the application's identity and uptime together with the reachability of every database it depends on. Answers without a session and is not rate limited, so it can be polled by a liveness probe.

200.description: Everything the application depends on is reachable

name.description: Organization-wide unique name for identifying the application

datetime.description: The application's current date and time incl. timezone

startup.description: The date and time of when the application instance started

uptime.description: The duration how long the application instance is running

hostname.description: Name of the host which is running the application instance

releaseId.description: The build running behind that version — the deployed commit. Absent when the deploy did not stamp one.

application.description: General information about application and current version

health.description: Global health status aggregated by groups

name.description: Unique name/identifier of the database system

essential.description: Database is essential for overall application health

latency.description: Latency or duration for full roundtrip in milliseconds

items.description: Detailed health information about a connected database

databases.description: Detailed health information about all connected databases

query.description: Newest first. The reader's own ideas are excluded unless asked for with author `mine`; without a status filter only open ideas appear. The search looks at titles and the ideas themselves.

post.summary: Post a story idea seeking writers

201.description: The idea is on the board

query.summary: One step of the story-idea carousel
query.description: The idea to show and the two either side of it, out of the open ideas the member has not read and did not write. Takes no filters: the set is the view's own. A missing neighbour is the end of the set, where the carousel stops rather than wrapping.

200.description: The step, and how many ideas the set holds

404.description: The anchor is not one of the ideas this carousel walks

get.summary: Read one story idea

404.description: No idea has this id

patch.description: Only the idea's author may change it, its status included. Absent fields stay as they are.

200.description: The idea as it now reads

403.description: The idea belongs to somebody else

404.description: No idea has this id

delete.summary: Take one's own story idea off the board

403.description: The idea belongs to somebody else

404.description: No idea has this id

post.summary: Start a conversation about a story idea
post.description: Creates a chat titled after the idea and invites its author — §11's public idea → private conversation. The author has to accept before anything is read, the same consent every chat invitation carries.

201.description: The new chat, with the author invited

403.description: The reader's own idea, or one that is closed

404.description: No idea has this id

put.summary: Mark an idea as read
put.description: The member's own record of having read somebody else's idea, and nothing more: keeping one to come back to is a favourite, which covers all six kinds. Idempotent, and it takes no body — read is the presence of the record, so unread is a DELETE.

404.description: No such idea

delete.summary: Set an idea back to unread
delete.description: Puts an idea back to unread. Answers the same way whether it was read or not, because unread is the absence of the record.

404.description: No such idea

query.summary: List the members whose contact this member refuses
query.description: Only the current user's own blocks; nobody can read whether somebody else blocked them.

post.summary: Refuse contact from a member
post.description: Neither member can invite the other afterwards, in either direction, and any invitation between them that is still unanswered is withdrawn. Nothing already shared is touched: a group or chat they are both in stays, and is left by leaving it. Blocking somebody already blocked changes nothing.

200.description: Contact from this member is refused

404.description: No such member

delete.summary: Allow contact from a member again
delete.description: Withdraws this member's own block. Invitations withdrawn when it was made are not restored — they were somebody's decision to make again.

404.description: This member is not blocked

post.summary: Report something to the operators
post.description: Files a report about a writing group, thread or post, a story idea, a chat or one of its messages, or a member. Only something the reporter can already see may be reported, and anything else answers 404 — so a report cannot be used to find out whether something exists. Reporting one's own account or one's own writing answers 403. What the reported thing said is copied into the report by the server, so the report is still readable to an operator after the content is deleted. Reporting the same thing again while the first report is still open rewrites its category and reason rather than filing a second.

404.description: No such thing, or the reporter may not see it

query.description: The operators' queue. Oldest first, so nothing waits at the bottom, and filterable by status, category and target type. Each report carries what the reported thing said when it was reported, so it stays readable after the content is gone, and whether that thing still exists.

patch.summary: Take a report, or close it
patch.description: Takes a report so other operators know it is in hand, or closes it with an outcome and a note saying what was decided. Both are recorded on the report itself, and a closed report is final — there is no reopening. Taking one somebody else already has is allowed and hands it over, so a forgotten claim cannot strand a report; closing it is reserved to whoever holds it.

404.description: No such report

409.description: The report is already closed, or another operator holds it and this is a closing. Refetching the queue shows the operator which of the two it was.

put.summary: Mark something as a favourite
put.description: The member's own favourite, visible to nobody else, on a group, a thread, a post, a story idea or a chat. Idempotent: favouriting twice is the same as favouriting once. Answers 404 for anything the member cannot see, so this cannot be used to find out that something exists.

404.description: No such thing, or the member cannot see it

delete.summary: Stop something being a favourite
delete.description: Answers the same way whether it was a favourite or not, because absent is the state being asked for. Unlike marking one, this asks no visibility question: a group that has gone private since is exactly the favourite a member most wants rid of.

query.description: Returns a page of members, narrowed to those whose username contains the search term when one is given. Only the id and the username are returned, never an email address.

patch.description: Every field is optional and none is ever required. An omitted field is left alone; an empty one is cleared. What a profile holds is readable by every member, so a field a member does not want read is one they leave empty.

200.description: The profile as it now stands

404.description: The account no longer exists — it was deleted between this request being authenticated and the update

put.summary: Set the member's own picture
put.description: Replaces whatever picture the member had. The image is re-encoded to one square WebP, which is also what strips its metadata; the original is never stored. `confirmed` is the member's declaration that they may use the picture, and `credit` says where it came from unless it is their own work.

422.description: Not a picture in a format we accept

delete.summary: Remove the member's own picture
delete.description: The member falls back to their initials. Idempotent: removing a picture that is not there is the same answer. The stored file is collected later rather than deleted here, so restoring a backup cannot produce a broken picture.

put.summary: Answer the optional profile questions
put.description: Sends the answers that changed. An entry with neither a text nor an option withdraws that answer, and the question then does not appear on the profile at all.

get.summary: Read a member's profile
get.description: The name and the date they joined. An operator additionally sees whether the account is banned; nobody else does. Reading one's own profile additionally carries how many Blind-Dates one has completed, which is sent to nobody else.

404.description: No member has this id

post.summary: Ban an account for breaking the platform rules
post.description: Ends every session the account has and refuses it from then on, at sign-in and on any session that outlives the ban. Deliberately not a deletion: the name and the address stay held, so the address cannot register again. Nothing the account wrote is removed — that is a separate act. An account holding a platform role cannot be banned; revoke the role first.

200.description: The account is banned and its sessions are ended

403.description: Not an operator, or the target holds a platform role and cannot be banned

404.description: No such account

409.description: The account is already banned

delete.summary: Lift a ban
delete.description: Restores access. Nothing is reclaimed, because nothing was released: the name and address were held throughout. The sessions ended at the ban and do not come back.

404.description: No such account, or it is not banned

get.summary: Read the optional profile questions this member answered

200.description: The answered questions, by section and then by position

get.summary: Read a picture
get.description: Served by the application rather than as a static file, so it is behind the same session check as everything else. The address changes whenever the picture does, so it is cached for a year.

404.description: No such picture

query.description: Returns a page of what has happened to the current user, newest first. A notification only exists while its recipient belongs to the group it is about, so nothing here needs filtering by access.

post.summary: Mark every notification as read
post.description: Opening the list is the act of having read it, so this marks all of the current user's unread notifications at once rather than one at a time.

post.summary: Start a chat
post.description: Creates a chat with the current user as its first member. Everybody else has to be invited and accept.

query.description: Returns a page of the chats the current user belongs to or has been invited to, most recently active first, each with how many messages they have not read.

post.summary: Invite somebody to a chat
post.description: Anybody already in the chat may invite. The invited member has to accept before they are part of the conversation.

403.description: The invitation has not been accepted

404.description: No such chat, or no such user

409.description: Already invited or already in the chat

query.summary: List who is in a chat
query.description: Everyone in the chat, including those who have been invited and not yet accepted. Visible to anybody the chat is visible to — an invitation has to be able to see who it would be joining.

404.description: No such chat, or not one of the current user's

post.summary: Accept an invitation to a chat

404.description: No invitation to accept

delete.summary: Leave a chat, or decline an invitation to one
delete.description: The same act either way. The last member out takes the chat and its messages with them.

404.description: Not in that chat

query.description: Returns a page of messages, newest first. Paged by cursor rather than offset: messages arrive while somebody reads, and an offset would repeat or skip whatever crossed the boundary.

403.description: The invitation has not been accepted

404.description: No such chat, or not one of the current user's

post.summary: Send a message

201.description: The message as it was stored

403.description: The invitation has not been accepted

404.description: No such chat, or not one of the current user's

post.summary: Mark a chat as read up to now
post.description: Everything already sent counts as read. Unread is a comparison against this moment, not a receipt per message.

403.description: The invitation has not been accepted

404.description: No such chat, or not one of the current user's

query.summary: Search groups, threads, pages, the public forum, story ideas and members at once
query.description: Runs one search across everything the current user may see and returns the matches grouped by kind, each with the total number found. A writing group's threads and pages and the public forum's are separate kinds, so neither can crowd the other out of a limit they shared. Story ideas include the reader's own and closed ones, which the interface labels. Posts, chat messages and next steps are not searched.

post.summary: Post a status update
post.description: A short remark on the logged-in home page.

query.description: The logged-in home page's feed, newest first, with each update's comment count. Paged by cursor rather than offset, the same reasoning as a chat's messages: a status posted while somebody reads would otherwise shift the window and make page two repeat or skip whatever crossed the boundary.

200.description: A page of status updates, newest first

get.summary: List a status update's comments
get.description: Oldest first, the way a conversation reads.

404.description: No such status update

post.summary: Comment on a status update

404.description: No such status update

get.summary: List every currently banned IP address

200.description: Every banned IP address, newest first

post.summary: Ban an IP address
post.description: Refuses every request from this address from now on, independent of any account. Deliberately not tied to banning an account: an address can belong to a household or a phone network, so the two are decided separately.

delete.summary: Lift an IP ban

200.description: The ban is lifted, or there was none

query.summary: Every member with the addresses they have been seen from
query.description: One row per member, including members with no session yet — the question is 'every member', and leaving those out would make it another one. `possibleAlts` names the other accounts sharing any of the same addresses, de-duplicated across them.

query.summary: Addresses more than one account has been seen from
query.description: The overview's question asked the other way round, and pre-filtered to the cases worth looking at. An address here is a reason to look, not a finding: a household, a school and a phone network behind CGNAT all put unrelated people on one address.

200.description: A page of shared addresses, most-shared first

get.summary: List every member on the watchlist
get.description: Not the report queue and not the strike history: nothing here has been decided, these are people somebody thought worth a second look.

200.description: Everyone currently watched, most recently added first

put.summary: Put a member on the watchlist
put.description: Idempotent: somebody already on it has their note and time updated rather than a second row added, which is why this is a PUT.

404.description: No such account

delete.summary: Take a member off the watchlist

200.description: Off the watchlist, or was never on it

get.summary: List every email domain blocked from registering

post.summary: Block an email domain from registering
post.description: Matched exactly, never as a suffix: blocking `mail.com` would otherwise take `gmail.com` with it. Blocking one already on the list updates its note.

delete.summary: Allow an email domain to register again

200.description: The domain may register again, or was never blocked

get.summary: Every word the community does not print
get.description: Alphabetical, because this is a list somebody reads to find out whether something is on it. The words are stored lower-cased; the match itself ignores case either way.

post.summary: Put a word on the list
post.description: Takes effect on everything already written, without any of it being rewritten — the mask is applied when text is read. Adding a word already on the list only refreshes its note.

200.description: The word is on the list

delete.summary: Take a word off the list
delete.description: Every text that held it becomes readable again exactly as it was written. Nothing was ever changed in storage, which is what makes this possible.

200.description: The word is off the list

get.summary: Who may work the Blind-Date desk
get.description: Everybody holding the right, and whether each is currently suspended by an application of their own. The first administrator holds it by being that account and is not in this list.

403.description: Only the first administrator may change this

put.summary: Give somebody the Blind-Date desk, or take it back
put.description: Only the first administrator, and only for somebody who is already an operator: a right that decides what an operator may reach means nothing to a member who cannot reach the moderation at all. `mayManage` false takes it away again.

403.description: Only the first administrator may change this

404.description: No member has this id

get.summary: The queue of open Blind-Date applications
get.description: Oldest first: whoever has waited longest is who the team should be looking at. Each row carries the preferences a pairing is judged on and the applicant's online time over the last thirty days.

post.summary: Put two applications together
post.description: Creates the group, both memberships, the first thread carrying the plot, and the pair — all in one transaction, so a half-made Blind-Date cannot exist. The group is private and its authors pseudonymous; revealing is the pair's own decision later.

200.description: The two are matched and the group exists

404.description: No such application, offer or account

409.description: One of them is already in a Blind-Date, excluded since applying, or both applications are the same member

post.summary: Decline an application
post.description: Kept as a declined row rather than deleted, like every other answer: who applied and how often is what the old spreadsheet carried implicitly. The note is for the team and is not shown to the applicant.

404.description: No such application, offer or account

get.summary: Name suspicions waiting for a decision
get.description: Raised automatically when one of the two usernames appears in a Blind-Date's exchange thread. **Nothing has happened yet**: the post is shown as written, both keep writing, and every consequence waits for confirmBlindDateSuspicion. A username can be an ordinary word, which is the whole reason a human decides.

post.summary: Confirm that somebody did give their name away
post.description: Only now do the consequences land: the Blind-Date ends, both seats are freed, the author is excluded and told by mail, and the other is told it ended without being told why. **Nothing is deleted** — the group, its threads and every post stay, and the two names are masked from then on.

200.description: The Blind-Date is ended and the consequences applied

404.description: No such application, offer or account

409.description: Somebody has already decided this one

post.summary: It was nothing
post.description: A username that happens to be an ordinary word, a coincidence. Nothing happens to anybody: the notice beside the post disappears and the Blind-Date carries on.

200.description: The suspicion is dismissed and nothing follows from it

404.description: No such application, offer or account

409.description: Somebody has already decided this one

get.summary: Who may not take part in Blind-Date
get.description: Its own list, deliberately not a flag on the watchlist: that list says of itself that it is neither an incident nor a consequence, and an exclusion is a consequence.

put.summary: Exclude a member from Blind-Date
put.description: Also withdraws whatever they have waiting: an application in the queue that can never be matched would be read again at every round. A Blind-Date already running is untouched — this lifts the bar for the next one, it does not end the current one.

404.description: No such application, offer or account

delete.summary: Let a member take part again

get.summary: Every offer, closed ones included
get.description: Unlike the members' own list, which shows only what is open: the team needs to see what it has already run.

post.summary: Offer a plot to apply for
post.description: Typically two are open at a time. Applying to one is not the only way in — a member may name any official RSH plot themselves.

patch.summary: Change an offer that is still open
patch.description: Every field at once, the same ones creating it takes. Only an open offer: a closed one is what somebody applied to and has to keep saying so. Applications keep the role text they chose, so editing the list cannot rewrite what anybody applied for.

404.description: No such application, offer or account

delete.summary: Close an offer
delete.description: Closed rather than deleted: applications point at it, and a closed offer still has to say what somebody applied for months later.

404.description: No such application, offer or account

get.summary: What members said about their Blind-Dates
get.description: The voluntary three-question form, newest first, with names — the point of reading it is to be able to ask somebody about what they wrote. Declines are in here too, with both answers empty: a form most people decline says something the answers cannot. The questions are about the format and never about the other person, so nothing here is a complaint about a member; those arrive as reports.

200.description: Every answer and every decline, newest first

query.summary: How each member's Blind-Dates have gone
query.description: One row per member who has been in at least one Blind-Date, with how many they saw through to the reveal, how many ended without one, how many of those they ended themselves, and how many are still running. Sorted by the ones they ended themselves, first: being left is not the same as leaving, and only the second is a pattern about this member. Operators only — the same figures next to one another are a ranking, which members are deliberately never shown.

200.description: A page of members and how their Blind-Dates went

get.summary: List everyone holding a platform role
get.description: Readable by any operator: knowing who else is on the team is not the same as being able to change it.

200.description: Administrators first, then moderators, each alphabetically

put.summary: Grant or revoke a platform role
put.description: Administrator only, because this is what changes the platform itself. `null` revokes, making the account an ordinary member again. Nobody may change their own role, which is what keeps the last administrator seat occupied. Granting or revoking `administrator` is reserved to the first administrator, and that account's own role cannot be changed by anybody — the database refuses it as well as this route.

403.description: Not an administrator, changing one's own role, granting a role to a banned account, touching the first administrator's role, or an ordinary administrator trying to grant or revoke `administrator`

404.description: No such account

get.summary: Which accounts a broadcast may be sent as
get.description: The first administrator, which is always available, followed by every released account in the order they are offered. Readable by every administrator, because this is the list a broadcast's sender is chosen from.

post.summary: Release an account as a sender
post.description: Only the first administrator, and by the name the account goes by rather than by its id: there is no way to look an account up, and the person doing this knows which persona they mean. Any account may be released, including one nobody signs in as — not the first administrator itself, which is available permanently.

403.description: Only the first administrator may change this

404.description: No account goes by this name

delete.summary: Withdraw a released sender
delete.description: Only the first administrator. What was already sent under that name is untouched: the sender is recorded on the publication itself, not read back from this list.

403.description: Only the first administrator may change this

get.summary: Count who a broadcast would reach
get.description: So the form can say how many before anybody presses send. A moment's truth rather than a promise: somebody may register in between.

200.description: How many members that audience holds

post.summary: Send one message to every member of an audience
post.description: Text, not HTML, like every other message this platform sends. The audience is chosen by group — administrators, moderators, ordinary members — because most of what an operator says is addressed to the team or to everybody but the team. Banned accounts are always left out; unverified addresses unless the audience says otherwise. Answers as soon as the recipients are known — the sending itself happens in the background, so a slow relay cannot hold the request open.

200.description: The messages are on their way

get.summary: List accounts that registered but never confirmed their address
get.description: Oldest first, because the account stuck longest is the one to look at. From their own side these accounts do not exist: an unverified session reaches nothing but the verification wall.

get.summary: Count how many members each inviter actually brought in
get.description: `arrived` counts registrations through that member's link whose address was confirmed — opening a link proves nothing, so only confirmed addresses are counted. `pending` are the ones that have not confirmed and are not counted as arrivals.

200.description: Members who have invited somebody, most arrivals first

post.summary: Send the verification mail again
post.description: Re-issues the ordinary verification link rather than a message of its own: the link is the point, and a second kind of mail carrying it would be a second place for it to go stale. The token cooldown still applies, so pressing this twice sends one mail.

200.description: The mail is on its way

404.description: No such account

409.description: That address is already confirmed

get.summary: Everyone with at least one strike, worst first
get.description: The overview the three-strikes area is grouped by. A member with a clean record is absent rather than listed with zeroes: the page is the ladder, and a whole membership under that heading would read as an accusation of everybody. `warnings` and `suspensions` are counts rather than a rung token — which section somebody is filed under is a question the interface answers, in German.

get.summary: Suggest the next step on the three-strikes ladder
get.description: Counts what was decided before and names the next rung: two warnings, then 24, 48 and 72 hours. A suggestion only — how heavily a violation weighs is a human decision, and any action may be taken regardless of what this returns, including skipping the ladder entirely.

get.summary: List a member's warnings and suspensions

200.description: Everything decided about this account, newest first

post.summary: Record a warning
post.description: Recorded, not enforced: a warning changes nothing about the account. It is what the next decision counts.

403.description: Not an operator, or the target holds a platform role and cannot be given a strike

404.description: No such account

post.summary: Suspend an account for a fixed number of hours
post.description: Ends every session and refuses the account until the moment it names, then lapses on its own with no cleanup. Deliberately not a ban: this one tells the member when it ends and why, because it is meant to correct.

403.description: Not an operator, or the target holds a platform role and cannot be given a strike

404.description: No such account

delete.summary: Lift a suspension before it lapses
delete.description: Restores access now. The history keeps the entry that imposed it: what was decided happened, whatever was decided afterwards.

404.description: No such account, or it is not suspended

get.summary: List a member's IP addresses, with shared accounts flagged
get.description: Every address this member has connected from, newest first, and for each one which other accounts have also used it. An empty `sharedWith` means nothing to flag. Addresses are shared often enough — a household, a phone network — that this is evidence to read rather than a verdict.

get.summary: List every page, public or not
get.description: Administrator only, unlike reading one: this is the list of what exists, including the pages that are not public.

put.summary: Create or rewrite a page
put.description: One route for both, because the slug is the identity: writing to one that does not exist yet is how a page is made. Changing a page's address is therefore making a different page, which is deliberate — the link somebody bookmarked should keep meaning what it meant.

delete.summary: Delete a page

404.description: No such page

get.summary: Read one page
get.description: A public page is readable by anybody, including somebody with no account. A page that is not public answers 404 rather than 403 to a reader without a session, so its existence stays hidden — the same rule the rest of the API follows.

404.description: No such page, or it is not readable without an account

get.summary: List the optional profile questions
get.description: The questions a profile may answer, by section and then by position. Readable by any member, because this is the form their own profile offers them.

200.description: Every question, with the options a choice question offers

post.summary: Add a profile question

put.summary: Rewrite a profile question
put.description: The options are replaced rather than merged. An option that goes away takes the answers naming it with it, which is the honest outcome: an answer pointing at a choice that no longer exists says nothing about the person who gave it.

404.description: No such question

delete.summary: Remove a profile question
delete.description: The answers go with it: they were answers to this question and to nothing else.

404.description: No such question

get.summary: List the forum's folders
get.description: Every folder of the public forum in creation order, flat. A folder the member may not see is absent rather than refused, and an operator sees all of them.

post.summary: Add a folder to the public forum
post.description: Operators only: the forum's structure has no owner below them, since it has no administrators. The permission it grants members is reduced by whatever is above it, so a folder cannot widen its parent. Nests at most 5 levels deep.

404.description: No such parent folder in the forum

422.description: The folder would nest too deeply

put.summary: Rename a folder of the public forum, or change its description
put.description: Operators only. A null description clears it, which is the only way back to none.

404.description: No such folder in the forum

delete.summary: Delete an empty folder of the public forum
delete.description: Operators only, and only when it holds nothing: no folder, thread or page. Removing what is inside it is #62's, not this.

404.description: No such folder in the forum

409.description: The folder still holds something

put.summary: Move a folder of the public forum, or take it to the root
put.description: Operators only. Everything inside it moves with it, and every permission below is reduced along the new path — so moving a room into a closed one closes what it holds. Refused when the target is the folder itself or something inside it, and when the subtree would reach past 5 levels, which depends on its deepest descendant.

404.description: No such folder in the forum, or no such target

422.description: The move would make a cycle, or nest too deeply

put.summary: Set what members may do with a folder, thread or page of the forum
put.description: Operators only, since the forum has no administrators. This is the row's *own* setting: whatever is above it can still close it, and re-opening that folder restores what was set here. Setting a folder's takes its whole subtree with it — `hidden` on a room hides everything in it, and answers 404 to a member rather than 403.

404.description: No such folder, thread or page in the forum

get.summary: List the forum's threads
get.description: Every thread of the public forum the member may see, most recently written in first. The tree nests them by `folderId`; a thread at the root has none.

post.summary: Start a thread in a folder the current user may write in
post.description: Members may start a thread where the folder grants `write`; operators may anywhere, the root included. A folder the member may not see answers 404 rather than 403.

404.description: No such folder, or the member may not see it

get.summary: Get one thread of the forum
get.description: The thread itself, without its posts. Hidden answers 404 rather than 403, so a member cannot tell a thread they may not see from one that does not exist.

404.description: No such thread, or the member may not see it

put.summary: Move a thread of the forum into another folder
put.description: Its author or an operator, and only into a folder they may write in — otherwise a member could drop a thread into a room that only reads. Its own permission travels with it; what the folder grants is applied on top.

404.description: No such thread or folder, or the member may not see it

query.summary: List the posts of a forum thread, plus the caller's own drafts
query.description: Returns a page of the thread's published posts, plus the current user's own unpublished drafts. Other members' drafts are never included.

404.description: No such thread, or the member may not see it

post.summary: Reply to a thread the current user may write in
post.description: Members may reply where the thread grants `write`; operators may anywhere. A thread the member may not see answers 404 rather than 403.

404.description: No such thread, or the member may not see it

patch.summary: Change a post, or publish a draft of one
patch.description: A post belongs to whoever wrote it, and only while they may still write in the thread — closing a folder freezes what was written in it. Autosaving a draft is this endpoint too.

200.description: The post as it now stands

404.description: No such thread or post, or the member may not see it

delete.summary: Remove a post
delete.description: Whoever wrote it, and only while they may still write in the thread. Discarding an unpublished draft is this endpoint too.

404.description: No such thread or post, or the member may not see it

get.summary: List the forum's pages
get.description: Every page of the public forum the member may see — announcements, FAQs, rules — most recently written in first, without their prose.

post.summary: Add a page to a folder the current user may write in
post.description: An announcement, an FAQ, the rules. Members may add one where the folder grants `write`; operators may anywhere, the root included.

404.description: No such folder, or the member may not see it

get.summary: Get one page of the forum
get.description: The page and its prose. Hidden answers 404 rather than 403, so a member cannot tell a page they may not see from one that does not exist.

404.description: No such page, or the member may not see it

put.summary: Rewrite a page of the forum
put.description: A page is written together rather than owned, so whoever may write here may change it — which is why this asks the page's own permission rather than who wrote it.

200.description: The page as it now stands

404.description: No such page, or the member may not see it

409.description: The page was saved by somebody else in the meantime

put.summary: Move a page of the forum into another folder
put.description: Whoever may write the page, and only into a folder they may write in. A page is written together rather than owned, so this asks the page's permission rather than who wrote it.

404.description: No such page or folder, or the member may not see it

get.summary: The plots the team is offering right now
get.description: Typically two at a time. A closed offer is history and stays out, and one past its deadline stays out too — except for the members who applied to it, who are still waiting on an answer. Applying to an offer is not the only way in, because a member may name any official RSH plot themselves.

get.summary: One offered plot, in full
get.description: What the card on the overview shortens. Open offers only — a closed one is no longer on the page the link came from.

200.description: The plot, with everything the team wrote about it

404.description: No such open offer

get.summary: The Blind-Dates that are running, without saying whose
get.description: How alive Blind-Date is right now, which is what makes people apply. A plot, how much has been written and when it last was — no names, no ids, and only the ones not yet revealed.

get.summary: The Blind-Date this member is in, if any
get.description: Only while it is still a Blind-Date: once revealed it is an ordinary group and answers 404 here. Carries whether each side has agreed to be revealed — never who the other is.

404.description: This member is not in a Blind-Date

delete.summary: End one's own Blind-Date without revealing
delete.description: Either of the two may end it, alone — unlike revealing, which needs both. Staying is not something either of them owes, and a way out that depended on the other person agreeing would depend on the person one is trying to get away from. Nothing is deleted: the group, its threads and everything both wrote stay as they are and stay pseudonymous. The other side is told that it ended, and nothing more.

200.description: The Blind-Date is over and both seats are free

404.description: No running Blind-Date to end

put.summary: Agree to be revealed
put.description: Refused until the two have written enough posts in the RPG thread together — the anonymity is meant to last long enough to be worth something. Both have to agree, and each says so for themselves. The second yes lifts the pseudonyms on the group — the same group, every post kept, nothing migrated. It does **not** make the group public: whether the writing is published stays the pair's own decision.

200.description: Recorded. The outcome says whether that was the second yes.

404.description: This member is not in a Blind-Date

409.description: The two have not written enough together yet. How many are still missing is on getOwnBlindDate.

delete.summary: Take that back
delete.description: While it can still be taken back — once both have agreed the group is already revealed. Nothing records that somebody withdrew: the question is only ever whether they want to now.

404.description: This member is not in a Blind-Date

get.summary: Whether this member may apply, and what they have
get.description: Asked before the form is shown, so it can explain itself rather than only refusing. It is not a permission: `createBlindDateApplication` checks the same thing again, because a check that only ran here is one anybody could skip.

get.summary: This member's own open application
get.description: Only their own, and only while it is open: an application that has been answered is the team's record rather than something to show back.

404.description: No open application

delete.summary: Withdraw the open application
delete.description: Recorded as withdrawn rather than deleted: who applied and thought better of it is part of what the queue says, and the team asked to keep every application.

404.description: No open application to withdraw

post.summary: Apply for a Blind-Date
post.description: Either taking up one of the offers or naming an official plot of one's own. One open application at a time, and one Blind-Date at a time — both refused here rather than left to the matching.

200.description: The application is in the queue

403.description: Excluded, already applied, already in a Blind-Date, or not enough online time

404.description: No such open offer

409.description: The offer no longer takes applications, or the role is not one it names

get.summary: The Blind-Date this member has not been asked about yet
get.description: The most recent one that is over, revealed or not, where this member has neither answered nor declined. Only the most recent: somebody coming back after three of them is asked about the one they remember rather than handed a queue of forms. 404 where there is nothing to ask about, which is the ordinary case.

200.description: A Blind-Date that has not been asked about

404.description: Nothing to ask about

post.summary: Answer the three questions, or decline them
post.description: Voluntary. Both answers together, or neither — sending neither is „nein danke“, which is recorded so the page stops asking. The questions are about the format and never about the other person; a complaint about somebody belongs in a report, which this is not. Answers reach the team and never the other member.

404.description: No such finished Blind-Date of this member's

409.description: This member has already answered about this one
